ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has one vertical bus on each of the left and right sides, the left side labeled B and the right side labeled A; between the two points there are three horizontal branches in parallel. Each branch contains a voltage source and a 5 Ω resistor; reading according to the source polarities in the figure, the source voltage terms corresponding to the direction from B to A for the three branches are +50 V, -30 V, -45 V respectively. There is switch S at the bottom, and the problem statement says S is open, so the bottom branch does not form a closed external path. Reasoning: Let U_AB = V_A - V_B, and according to the specified method take the three branch currents as being in the direction from B to A. Then I1 = (50 - U_AB)/5, I2 = (-30 - U_AB)/5, I3 = (-45 - U_AB)/5. Since switch S is open, there is no external current path between terminals A and B, so write KCL for the parallel network: I1 + I2 + I3 = 0. Substituting gives (50 - U_AB)/5 + (-30 - U_AB)/5 + (-45 - U_AB)/5 = 0, namely (50 - 30 - 45) - 3U_AB = 0. Therefore 3U_AB = -25, U_AB = -25/3 V.

method.method_draft: Let U_AB=V_A−V_B. For the three parallel branches, write currents from B to A as I1=(50−U_AB)/5, I2=(-30−U_AB)/5, and I3=(-45−U_AB)/5 using the polarities read from the image. Since switch S is open, there is no external path, so KCL gives I1+I2+I3=0. Solve (50−U_AB)+(-30−U_AB)+(-45−U_AB)=0 to obtain U_AB=(50−30−45)/3=−25/3 V.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct nodal/KCL route: treat the three source-resistor branches as parallel Thevenin branches and use the open-switch condition that no external current enters either terminal. It is the natural single-solution method for this circuit.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read from the figure that A and B are the right and left rails of a three-branch parallel network; the bottom switch S is open, so it does not short A to B. Each branch contains a voltage source in series with a 5 Ω resistor. From the battery long-plate polarities, assign the source voltages from B to A as +50 V for the top branch and −30 V, −45 V for the middle and bottom branches.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the text condition “switch S is open” and the requested quantity U_AB between points A and B; no additional numerical values come from the text beyond the labels already shown in the figure.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use KVL for each branch and KCL at the two-terminal network under open-circuit conditions. For a branch with signed source emf E from B to A and resistance R, the current from B to A is I=(E-U_AB)/R, and because the terminals are open, the algebraic sum of the three branch currents is zero.
